title: pinning-and-telemetry-tactics-journal
content:
Purpose: quick personal journal + working notes for telem-driven model pin/unpin strategies and micro-rollout tactics. Not a canonical playbook — this is my scratchpad for experiments and hypotheses to formalize later.

High-level intent:
- Reduce noisy, manual rollbacks by surfacing compact, machine-readable signals to decide pin/unpin and traffic-steer changes.
- Keep a minimal set of actionable metrics (latency P95/P99, request-error-rate, hallucination-rate-proxy, cost-per-1000-tokens) that can run automated gates.
- Add short circuit for severe regressions: immediate pin of last-stable and notify SRE/Ownership.

Key concepts / heuristics I want to try:
1) Fractional pin buckets (0%, 1%, 5%, 20%, 50%) instead of single canary. Move on a thermostat of rolling window signals rather than single-point spikes.
2) Traffic cohesion: pin by client cohort (tenant, SDK-version, region) not just global percentage. Warm cohorts before bumping fraction.
3) Composite signal threshold: require 2 of 3 to trip (latency-surge, error-rate uplift, quality-drop) with different weights depending on fraction.

Minimum metric set (derive these from existing exporters / e2e agents):
- inference.req.count (per model-version, per cohort)
- inference.latency.p95 / p99
- inference.errors.per_1k (5xx, timeout, inference-timeout)
- quality.hallucination.proxy_rate (proxy from synthetic eval set + in-prod golden prompts)
- kvcache.hit_rate (indicates inefficient cache causing latency)
- cost.per_1k_tokens (only used for advisory signals)

PromQL snippets to prototype (handy):
- p95: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(inference_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, model_version, cohort))
- error-rate: sum(rate(inference_errors_total{code!~"2.."}[5m])) by (model_version, cohort) / sum(rate(inference_requests_total[5m])) by (model_version, cohort)

Automated gate sketch (pseudocode):
- for each cohort:
  - compute baseline from rolling 7d median for p95, error-rate, quality.
  - if (p95 > baseline * 1.6) and (error-rate > baseline + 2ppt): mark cohort as "hot" -> immediately cut fraction to previous safe fraction and pin that cohort to last-stable.
  - else if (2 of 3 signals exceed thresholds for 15m sustained): hold progression and notify owner via #release-alerts, schedule 20m re-eval.

Quick checklist for a pin/unpin run (manual fallback):
- [ ] Confirm last-stable model_version tag and docker image id (cmd: rdcli model versions --recent)
- [ ] Snapshot KPI baseline (run queries, store outputs)
- [ ] Create canary cohort mapping in routing config (client-cohort -> fraction)
- [ ] Enable synthetic golden-set sampling for that cohort (link the golden set id)
- [ ] Start with 1% (or cohort minimum), observe 30m.
- [ ] If stable, step to 5% then 20% (each step wait 30m and pass automated gate).
- [ ] If auto-gate trips: pin cohort, rollback traffic for cohort, escalate (pager / #oncall).

Observability / alerting suggestions (short):
- Implement a "rollout-inspector" dashboard with heatmap: rows = cohorts, cols = time slices; cells show delta from baseline for p95 and error-rate. Color thresholds: amber (20% upl), red (50%+).
- Add a composite index metric rollout.safety_index per cohort (0..100) computed as weighted sum of normalized anomalies. Alert when < 30.

Rollback / escape hatch commands (ops crib notes):
- pin model_version X for tenant Y: rdcli tenant pin --tenant Y --model-version X
- route all traffic to stable for region eu-west1: rdcli routing set --region eu-west1 --model-version stable-2025-09-14
- quick traffic siphon to shadow bucket: rdcli route adjust --name siphon-temp --fraction 0.9 --target shadow

Synthetic traffic plan for validation:
- Use the "mini-symphony" runner to generate 100 requests/min of realistic prompts per cohort for 30 min (script: infra/tools/mini-symphony/run.sh --cohort prod-sdk-v2 --payload golden.json)
- Compare model outputs against golden-set using string-similarity + classifier probe for hallucination.

Open questions / experiments to run:
- Q1: how sensitive is the composite gate to low QPS cohorts? Need min-requests threshold to avoid noisy triggers. Proposal: require >= 200 reqs in 15m window or fall back to longer window aggregation.
- Q2: Should we treat cache degradation as first-class separate signal and route low-cache-hit cohorts to a different model variant that warms slower? Might reduce noise.
- Q3: can we use shadow-based A/B to compute true delta in hallucination rate before exposing to users? Costy but useful for high-risk models.
- Q4: best escalation path for non-prod tenants that mirror prod — allow automated pin with delayed human notify (e.g., 10m hold) vs immediate manual.

Mini experiments to prioritize (todo):
- [ ] Implement rollout.safety_index prototype in prometheus recording rules (owner: Sofia) — target: reduce manual pager volume for small regressions.
- [ ] Run live micro-rollout for model v2026-01-beta on two low-risk cohorts (billing-test, internal-staging) with golden sampling enabled (owner: Evan).
- [ ] Bench synthetic runner thresholds to validate min-requests heuristics (owner: Maya).

Notes from last run (2026-01-22):
- Ran 1% -> 5% -> 20% progression on v2026-01-beta for cohort internal-staging. At 5% saw p99 jump 2.2x but error-rate stayed flat. Composite index dropped to 36 but gate did not auto-trip because quality probe showed no hallucinations. Manual hold and re-eval for 40m revealed kvcache hit_rate slipped (warm-up issue). Resolution: added forced pre-warm for that cohort (warmup=true in route config) and re-ran, p99 normalized.

Messaging / comms template (for slack alert to owners):
- Subject: [Rollout Alert] model v{ver} cohort {cohort} — safety_index {val}
- Body: Observed p95/p99 uplift: {p95_delta}, error-rate: {err_delta}, quality_delta: {qual_delta}. Suggested action: {pin|hold|progress}. Link to rollout-inspector: {url} and last-stable: {last-stable-tag}.

Quick heuristics cheatsheet (for myself):
- If p99 > 2x baseline -> immediate cohort pin.
- If safety_index < 30 -> hold progression and notify (15m re-eval).
- If hallucination_delta > 1ppt absolute -> pin and schedule immediate QA review.
- If kvcache hit_rate drops > 20% -> consider warmup + slower fraction ramp.

Final thought: need to formalize which signals are "safety-critical" (auto-pinning allowed) vs "operator-review" (notify only). My current inclination: latency (p99) and error-rate = safety-critical; quality/hallucination = operator-review but fast pin if verified by synthetic golden-set probe.

Random TODO in doc: draft a short RFC proposing rollout.safety_index and the cohort-bucket approach. If we can get a recording rule + dashboard + 1 automation rule for pin/unpin we can test for a month before rolling out to all teams.

-- Evan
